claims.planned: Declarative config (YAML) of prompts x providers x test cases with assertions
claims.finding: The docs explicitly describe a YAML configuration format that runs prompts × providers × test cases as a matrix. The 'x' (cross-product) framing is used directly.
claims.quote: The YAML configuration format runs each prompt through a series of example inputs (aka 'test case') and checks if they meet requirements (aka 'assertions').

claims.planned: Running prompts x providers produces a matrix view
claims.finding: The docs use 'matrix view' explicitly for comparing prompts across providers.
claims.quote: Running `promptfoo eval` over this config will result in a _matrix view_ that you can use to evaluate GPT vs Gemini.

claims.finding: The docs split assertion types into two named categories: 'Deterministic Eval Metrics' (programmatic, run directly on output) and 'Model-Assisted Eval Metrics' (leverage language models). Both categories are explicitly documented with full lists.
claims.quote: Assertions are used to compare the LLM output against expected values or conditions.

claims.finding: The taxonomy is extensive. Deterministic types include string matching (equals, contains, regex, starts-with), structured data (is-json, is-sql, is-xml, is-html), custom logic (javascript, python, ruby, webhook), text quality metrics (rouge-n, bleu, levenshtein), performance (latency, cost), function call validation, agent tracing (trajectory:tool-used, trace-span-count), safety (guardrails), and refusal detection (is-refusal). Model-graded types include: similar (embeddings), llm-rubric, g-eval, factuality, answer-relevance, context-faithfulness, context-recall, select-best, and trajectory:goal-success. All deterministic types support 'not-' prefix negation.
claims.quote: All deterministic types support negation: prepend 'not-' to create inverse assertions (e.g., `not-equals`).

claims.finding: Red-teaming is a first-class feature. The docs describe three attack categories (privacy/PII leakage, prompt injection, jailbreaking), black-box and white-box testing modes, and a plugin system covering harmful content, authorization flaws (BOLA/BFLA), competitor endorsement, and more. Output is a quantified risk report.
claims.quote: Promptfoo identifies vulnerabilities in AI systems through 'simulated adversarial inputs' before deployment, enabling teams to 'produce a report that quantifies the risk of misuse.'

teachable_points.point: promptfoo is described as an open-source CLI and library, not just a GUI tool. It integrates with CI/CD (GitHub Actions mentioned) for automated evaluation on every change.
teachable_points.quote: an open-source CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps
teachable_points.numbers: Supports CI/CD integration; GitHub Actions named explicitly

teachable_points.point: The cross-product (matrix) evaluation is a core design primitive. Test variables defined as arrays produce all combinations automatically.
teachable_points.numbers: N prompts × M providers × K test cases = N×M×K evaluations

teachable_points.point: Performance features — caching, concurrency, and live reloading — are built in to speed up the eval loop.
teachable_points.quote: Speed up evaluations with caching, concurrency, and live reloading

teachable_points.point: Red-teaming distinguishes black-box testing (only inputs/outputs observable, simulates real-world attacks) from white-box testing (full access to architecture, training data, weights).
teachable_points.quote: Black Box Testing: treats 'the LLM as a closed system, where only inputs and outputs are observable,' simulating real-world attack scenarios.

teachable_points.point: Agent and tracing assertions are a modern addition enabling evaluation of multi-step agentic behavior: tool usage order, argument matching, step counts, trace span duration.
teachable_points.quote: trajectory:tool-used, trajectory:tool-args-match, trajectory:tool-sequence, trajectory:step-count, trace-span-count, trace-span-duration, trace-error-spans

teachable_points.point: Model-graded assertions include embeddings-based similarity (not just LLM-as-judge rubrics) and RAG-specific metrics: context-faithfulness, context-recall, context-relevance, answer-relevance.

misconceptions_to_avoid: promptfoo is not only for prompt testing — red-teaming/security scanning is an equal first-class feature described on the intro page.
Not all assertions invoke an LLM. The majority of built-in types are fully deterministic (string ops, JSON validation, regex, latency, cost checks).
The config format is not just a list of test cases — it defines a full cross-product matrix of prompts × providers × test cases, producing a 'matrix view' output.
Model-graded assertions are not synonymous with 'LLM-as-judge rubrics' — the category also includes embeddings-based similarity (similar) and RAG-specific retrieval metrics.

Red-teaming 'prompt injection' and 'jailbreaking' are defined as distinct attack types: prompt injection chains untrusted input with trusted prompts; jailbreaking subverts foundational safety filters.
notes_for_authors: All core claims confirmed from live docs. The assertion taxonomy is more extensive than a simple deterministic/model-graded split suggests — consider calling out the agent tracing assertions as evidence that eval tooling has evolved for agentic systems. The 'not-' prefix negation for all deterministic types is a clean pedagogical point. The YAML matrix view quote is the sharpest illustration of the cross-product concept and worth using verbatim.
